name: Case Report Checklist
source: Owner-supplied checklist (StewardMD, 2026-11-24), provided in place of the CC BY-NC-ND official text.
licence: Owner-supplied text for StewardMD ResearchMD use
instructions: Tick each item after confirming that the corresponding information is adequately addressed in the manuscript.
finalCheck: Check that the manuscript is internally consistent, patient details are de-identified, all reported investigations and interventions are accurately described, and the target journal's author instructions are followed.

items.text: State the principal diagnosis, clinical condition or intervention being reported, and include the words "Case Report" in the title.
Provide 2-5 terms that identify the main diagnosis or intervention and include "Case Report" as one of the keywords.
Briefly explain what is distinctive about the case and what useful information it contributes to the medical literature. Do not cite references in the abstract.
Summarise the patient's principal symptoms and the most important clinical findings.
State the main diagnosis, key therapeutic measures and the resulting clinical outcome.
State the central lesson or practical message that readers should take away from the case.
Explain the clinical context and why the condition or presentation is relevant.
Summarise in approximately one or two paragraphs why this case is noteworthy or unusual.
Clarify what makes the case distinctive and how it may add to existing knowledge; relevant references may be included.
Present relevant patient-specific information while removing identifying details.
Describe the patient's main complaints, symptoms and reason for seeking care.
Include pertinent medical, family and psychosocial history, together with relevant genetic information.
Describe relevant treatments or procedures received before the current episode and their outcomes.
Describe the important findings from the physical examination and any other clinically significant observations.
Arrange the relevant past and current events from the episode of care in chronological order, showing the progression from presentation through assessment, treatment and outcome.
Report the relevant assessments and tests, including physical examination, laboratory investigations, imaging and validated surveys or other assessments, as applicable.
Describe obstacles affecting the diagnostic process, such as limited access to investigations, financial constraints or cultural factors.
State the final diagnosis and identify other diagnoses that were considered.
Include the relevant prognostic assessment, disease stage or severity classification where applicable (for example, cancer staging).
Describe the treatment provided, including drug therapy, surgery, preventive measures, procedures or self-care interventions, as relevant.
Specify the details needed to understand the intervention, including medication name, dose or strength, route and duration, where applicable.
Record any alteration, addition or discontinuation of an intervention and explain the reason for the change.
Report outcomes assessed by the treating clinician and by the patient, if available.
Include important results from repeat diagnostic tests and other follow-up assessments.
Describe whether the patient followed the intervention and how adherence and tolerability were evaluated.
Document any complications, adverse effects or unanticipated events during the course of care.
Provide a balanced discussion of the scientific strengths of the report and its limitations.
Discuss previously published medical evidence relevant to the case and support the discussion with references.
Explain the scientific reasoning behind the conclusions, including assessment of possible causes or mechanisms where relevant.
End with a concise paragraph stating the main lessons from the case; do not include references in this concluding paragraph.
Include the patient's own account, in approximately one or two paragraphs, describing their perspective on the treatment or treatments received.
Confirm whether the patient provided informed consent for publication.
Ensure that consent documentation can be provided if requested.
